get.summary: List the login methods this deployment offers
get.description: Lists one descriptor per login method that takes part and is not turned off by the deployment, sorted by method name, together with whether a first login may open an account and the second-factor kinds the deployment takes in. It reads no credential and no request body, so every caller gets the same document. A method turned off by the deployment is left out rather than reported with a flag, and the call answers 503 when the settings that decide which methods are off cannot be read. Enterprise identity providers are not listed here; they are discovered through the SSO module.

200.description: A descriptor per method taking part, whether registration is open, and the factor kinds the deployment offers

503.description: The settings that turn methods off could not be read

post.summary: Start a login flow for one method
post.description: Starts a login flow for the method named in the body and advances it through the method's first step. The flow token is written to the flow cookie, or, with `binding` set to `header`, returned in `flow_token` with no cookie; later calls are bound to the flow by that token. The route reads no cookie, so a stale session cookie does not prevent a login. Depending on the method and the multi-factor policy, the returned flow may already stand at a second-factor, enrollment or ready step. A body that is not `application/json` is a 415, an unknown member or a value outside its domain is a 400, and a credential the method did not accept is a 401 login-failed — except two refusals the route answers as a 400: a phone prefix the deployment does not allow (`unsupported-region`) and an identifier that cannot name an account (`bad-request`). A 429 carries `Retry-After` when the back-off states a delay.

requestBody.description: The start request: the method to run, how the flow token is carried, where to return after a completed login, and the fields the method's first step takes. The body must be `application/json`, is limited to 64 KiB, and refuses unknown members.

schema.description: The start request; `method` must name a login method this deployment takes in, or the call is a bad request.

method.description: The stable name of a login method, as returned in `name` by `GET /auth/methods`. A name the deployment does not take in is a 400 bad-request; a method turned off by the deployment is a 403 method-disabled.

purpose.description: Accepted but not read by this route: a flow started here always has the purpose login. Use `POST /auth/flows/authenticated` for link, step-up or enroll.

delivery.description: How a completed login is delivered: `session` (the default) sets the session cookie and answers the session view; `token` answers an access and refresh token pair. `token` must be enabled by the deployment and requires the token capability, otherwise the request is a 400 bad-request.

return_to.description: Where to send the user agent after a callback login completes: either a path starting with a single `/`, not `//`, without backslash, control characters or `@` and at most 2048 bytes, or an absolute URL whose origin the deployment trusts. Anything else is a 400 bad-request. The value is stored in the flow record, and no parameter of the callback request can change it.

binding.description: How the flow token is carried: `cookie` (the default) writes the flow cookie (`__Host-authn-flow`, or `authn-flow` when insecure use is allowed) and returns no token in the body; `header` returns the token in `flow_token` and sets no cookie, so the client must send it in the `Authn-Flow` request header on every later call. A callback navigation cannot set a header, so a flow bound this way cannot finish a redirect method.

input.description: The fields the method's first step takes, as name-to-value strings. At most 8 members, each value at most 512 bytes; anything beyond is a 400 bad-request.

200.description: The flow, advanced to its first step

400.description: The body could not be read, a value is outside its domain, or the method refused the identifier as a region the deployment does not serve (`unsupported-region`) or as one that cannot name an account (`bad-request`)

403.description: The method or the account is unavailable

409.description: The request conflicts with the account's state

415.description: The request body is not application/json

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

post.summary: Start a flow on the identity already signed in
post.description: Starts a `link`, `step-up` or `enroll` flow on the identity the gateway authenticated and advances it to its first step. The flow is bound to that account and session, and an impersonating identity is refused with 403 impersonation-restricted. A link and an enrollment require the fresh authentication the account's factors call for — a fresh local multi-factor when the account holds an active factor, a fresh first factor otherwise — and answer 401 insufficient_user_authentication with `WWW-Authenticate` when it does not hold. A step-up whose account holds at least one factor usable for this session starts at the second factor and answers the offered factors without calling the method; an account that holds factors but none usable for this session — because each was activated at or after the session authenticated — is refused with 401 insufficient_user_authentication, and an account with no factor starts at the first factor with the method named in the body. The delivery mode is not read from the body: it follows the kind of the request's session.

requestBody.description: The request to start a link, step-up or enrollment flow: the purpose, the method and fields where the purpose takes them, how the flow token is carried, and the return target. The body must be `application/json`, is limited to 64 KiB, and refuses unknown members.

schema.description: The start request for a purpose other than login; `purpose` must be `link`, `step-up` or `enroll`.

method.description: The method to run for `link`, and for a `step-up` of an account that holds no factor. For an enrollment it is not read, and for a step-up the policy answers with usable factors it is not read either; a step-up whose account holds factors but none usable for this session is refused with 401 insufficient_user_authentication before the method is consulted. A name the deployment does not take in is a 400 bad-request.

purpose.description: Required, and one of `link`, `step-up` or `enroll`: bind an external identity, strengthen the current session, or register a factor. Any other value, including an empty one, is a 400 bad-request.

return_to.description: Where to send the user agent after a callback login completes: either a path starting with a single `/`, not `//`, without backslash, control characters or `@` and at most 2048 bytes, or an absolute URL whose origin the deployment trusts. Anything else is a 400 bad-request. The value is stored in the flow record, and no parameter of the callback request can change it.

binding.description: How the flow token is carried: `cookie` (the default) writes the flow cookie (`__Host-authn-flow`, or `authn-flow` when insecure use is allowed) and returns no token in the body; `header` returns the token in `flow_token` and sets no cookie, so the client must send it in the `Authn-Flow` request header on every later call. A callback navigation cannot set a header, so a flow bound this way cannot finish a redirect method.

input.description: The fields the started step takes, as name-to-value strings: the method's first step for `link`, the enrollment step for `enroll` where `kind` names the factor kind, and nothing for a step-up that starts at the second factor. At most 8 members, each value at most 512 bytes.

200.description: The flow, advanced to its first step

400.description: The body could not be read, or a value is outside its domain

403.description: The method or the account is unavailable

409.description: The request conflicts with the account's state

415.description: The request body is not application/json

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

post.summary: Answer the current step of the flow the request is bound to
post.description: Advances the flow the request is bound to by one step. The body must echo the flow's current `seq`, or the call is a 401 flow-invalid. `step` must be one of `answer`, `factor`, `enroll` or `complete`: a name outside that set is a 400 bad-request, and a step the flow's state does not accept is a 401 flow-invalid. A flow accepts at most eight client answers, after which it is moved to failed and every later answer is a 401 flow-invalid. The answer is the flow at its next step or, once the flow is ready, the completed result: the session view, the token pair, or the `linked`/`enrolled` result of a link or enrollment. Each step is a compare-and-swap on the flow record, so concurrent answers are decided by the store and the loser gets 401 flow-invalid rather than a retry.

requestBody.description: One answer to the bound flow: the step number to echo, the step being answered, and the fields that step takes. The body must be `application/json`, is limited to 64 KiB, and refuses unknown members.

schema.description: One answer to the bound flow: which step is being answered, the step number to echo, and the fields the step takes.

seq.description: The `seq` of the flow as last returned. It must equal the record's current step number; a stale or future value is a 401 flow-invalid.

step.description: The step being answered: `answer` for a first-factor submission, only while the flow is at the first factor; `factor` for a second-factor step, only at the second factor; `enroll` for an enrollment step, only at the enroll state; `complete` to take the result of a ready flow. A name outside this set is a 400 bad-request, and a step that does not match the flow's state is a 401 flow-invalid.

input.description: The fields the step takes, as name-to-value strings. At most 8 members, each value at most 8 KiB; a second-factor step reads `factor` to choose the factor and then the values that factor asks for, an enrollment step reads `kind`, and `complete` reads nothing.

200.description: The flow advanced, or completed with a session or a token pair

schema.description: One of four shapes, told apart by `state` and the members present: an open flow, a completed login delivered as a session, a completed login delivered as a token pair or an elevated step-up, or the result of a link or enrollment.

400.description: The body could not be read, or a value is outside its domain

401.description: The credential did not hold, or the flow binding is missing or wrong

403.description: The method or the account is unavailable

409.description: The request conflicts with the account's state: a completed link names an external identity another account already holds. A step that does not match the flow's state is a 401 flow-invalid, not a 409.

415.description: The request body is not application/json

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

get.summary: The state of the flow the request is bound to
get.description: Reads the flow the request is bound to so a client can resume it, for example after a page refresh or after a callback sent the user agent back. The flow token is taken from the flow cookie or the `Authn-Flow` header, and a flow bound by the header gets it echoed in `flow_token`. A missing or mismatched binding, and a flow that is done, failed or gone, are all answered 401 flow-invalid. The reply is built from the stored record alone, so a first-factor step the method named cannot be re-prompted with its fields and its `next.kind` is `challenge`.

200.description: The flow's current step, so a page refresh can resume

401.description: The flow binding is missing or wrong, or the flow is done or gone

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

503.description: The flow store could not be reached

delete.summary: Abandon the flow the request is bound to
delete.description: Removes the flow the request is bound to and clears the flow cookie. The flow token is read from the cookie or the `Authn-Flow` header. A request with no binding, with a wrong binding, or naming a flow that is already gone is answered the same 401 flow-invalid, while a request that removes a live flow answers 204; no session, token or account state is touched.

401.description: The flow binding is missing or wrong, or the flow is gone

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

503.description: The flow store could not be reached

get.summary: Handle a provider's callback as a browser navigation
get.description: Handles a provider's callback as a top-level browser navigation. The callback is bound through the flow cookie only, because a navigation cannot set a request header; the path's provider must equal the provider recorded in the flow and the flow must be at its first factor, otherwise the call is a 401 flow-invalid before any method is asked. The engine moves the flow to processing before calling the method, so a replayed authorization code or assertion loses the compare-and-swap and gets 401 flow-invalid. A GET callback that carries no flow cookie is always 401 flow-invalid: an identity-provider-initiated sign-in is served only as a POST. A cookie login that completes on this route answers 303 to the flow's stored return target instead of a body.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: The provider this callback is for: a social method's stable name, or, for an enterprise SSO provider, the identifier the start named in `input.provider`. It must equal the provider recorded in the flow the callback is bound to; a mismatch is a 401 flow-invalid and the callback never reaches a method.

200.description: The flow, advanced by the callback

303.description: The user agent is sent to the flow's stored return target instead of being answered a body: a completed cookie login writes its session cookie in this response, and a flow that still needs a second factor or an enrollment keeps the flow cookie and resumes with `GET /auth/flows/current`

401.description: The flow binding is missing or wrong

403.description: The method or the account is unavailable

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

post.summary: Handle a provider's callback as a cross-site form post
post.description: Handles a provider's callback delivered as a cross-site form post, which is how SAML's assertion consumer service is reached. The callback is bound through the flow cookie only, because a form post cannot set a request header; the path's provider must equal the provider recorded in the flow and the flow must be at its first factor, otherwise the call is a 401 flow-invalid before any method is asked. The posted form is bounded to 512 KiB before it is parsed, and a body over that bound is answered 401 login-failed with the flow left a tombstone. The engine moves the flow to processing before calling the method, so an assertion is handled at most once. Without a flow cookie the route serves an identity-provider-initiated sign-in, but only for an enterprise provider whose row enables it.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: The provider this callback is for: a social method's stable name, or, for an enterprise SSO provider, the identifier the start named in `input.provider`. It must equal the provider recorded in the flow the callback is bound to; a mismatch is a 401 flow-invalid and the callback never reaches a method.

200.description: The flow, advanced by the callback

303.description: The user agent is sent to the flow's stored return target instead of being answered a body: a completed cookie login writes its session cookie in this response, and a flow that still needs a second factor or an enrollment keeps the flow cookie and resumes with `GET /auth/flows/current`

401.description: The flow binding is missing or wrong

403.description: The method or the account is unavailable

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

put.description: Changes the caller's password. The call requires the fresh authentication every change of what proves the account asks for — a fresh local multi-factor when the account holds an active factor, a fresh first factor otherwise — and refuses an impersonating identity with 403 impersonation-restricted. The current password may be empty for an account that signed up through a provider and holds no password; a wrong one is a 401 login-failed, and a new password outside the password module's policy is a 400 bad-request. On success the current session is rotated to a new token, the account's other sessions are revoked, and the answer is 204 with the new session cookie set. An account that has neither a username nor a verified email is refused with 409 login-identifier-required.

requestBody.description: The current and new passwords. `new_password` is required and `current_password` may be empty. The body must be `application/json` and refuses unknown members.

schema.description: The password change: the password the account has now, when it has one, and the new one.

current_password.description: The password the account has now. Empty or absent is allowed for an account that signed up through an external provider and holds no password; a wrong value is a 401 login-failed.

new_password.description: The new password, required and non-empty. The password module decides the policy: a value outside it is a 400 bad-request, and a value equal to the current password is refused.

400.description: The new password is outside the policy

401.description: No usable credential, or the current password did not hold

403.description: The identity is impersonating, which the route refuses

409.description: The request conflicts with the account's state

415.description: The request body is not application/json

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

post.summary: Send a code to a phone number being added to the account
post.description: Sends a verification code to a phone number the caller wants to add to the account, and answers how long the code lives and how soon another may be sent, both in whole seconds. The answer carries no challenge identifier and no hint whether the number already belongs to another account: a number another account holds is sent a code exactly as a free one is, and the conflict surfaces only when the verified number is written. The pending verification is held against the caller's session, so one session has at most one and a later call replaces it. The route is present only in an assembly that takes in the SMS code capability. A key-value store that cannot be read is a 503 before any code is sent; a store that cannot be written after the code went out is also a 503, and the code then cannot be verified.

requestBody.description: The phone number to send a verification code to. The body must be `application/json` and refuses unknown members.

schema.description: The phone number to send a verification code to.

phone.description: The number in international E.164 form: a leading `+`, a non-zero country digit, then 6 to 14 more digits. The value is not parsed, completed or reformatted, so a national-format number is a 400 bad-request.

200.description: The challenge, and when the code may be resent

400.description: The body could not be read, or the number is outside its domain

403.description: The identity is impersonating, which the route refuses

415.description: The request body is not application/json

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

post.summary: Verify the code sent to a phone number
post.description: Verifies the code sent to the pending number and binds that number to the caller's account as an identifier verified by SMS code, replacing a phone the account already has. The number and the challenge are taken from the server-side record of the caller's session, not from the request, so a client cannot choose which number is verified. The number's back-off is checked before the code is compared, so a number in back-off answers 429 without offering the code to a guess; a wrong code is a 401 login-failed and counts against the number, and a correct one clears the back-off. On success the pending record is consumed, the caller's session token is rotated, the account's other sessions are revoked, and the answer is 204. A missing pending record, or one that names another account, is a 401 flow-invalid.

requestBody.description: The verification code the SMS channel delivered. The body must be `application/json` and refuses unknown members.

schema.description: The verification code sent to the pending phone number.

code.description: The code as the SMS channel sent it. Empty or longer than 32 bytes is a 400 bad-request before any comparison; a wrong code is a 401 login-failed and counts against the number.

204.description: The number was verified and added to the account

400.description: The body could not be read, or the code is empty or longer than 32 bytes

403.description: The identity is impersonating, which the route refuses

409.description: The number belongs to another account

415.description: The request body is not application/json

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

delete.summary: Remove one of the caller's own identifiers
delete.description: Removes one login identifier the caller's account holds. The identifier must be the caller's own: one that does not exist and one that belongs to another account are answered identically as a 400 bad-request, so the route discloses nothing about what another account holds. The call requires the fresh authentication every change of what proves the account asks for and refuses an impersonating identity. The route does not check whether the identifier is the account's last way to sign in, so the last one can be removed; that rule belongs to unbinding an external identity. Unlike the routes that add a way in, this one does not revoke the caller's other sessions, and it publishes no event of its own: `authn.identifier.changed` is published by the account module on the removal.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The identifier's identifier, as returned in the `id` of one of the caller's own identifiers. A value the caller's account does not hold, including one another account holds, is a 400 bad-request.

403.description: The identity is impersonating, which the route refuses

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

post.summary: Add one of the caller's own login identifiers
post.description: Adds one login identifier to the caller's account. `kind=username` writes a login name at once, recorded as the account's own assertion; `kind=email` sends a code to the address and answers `state: pending` with how long the code lives and how soon another may be sent, and the address is written only after `POST /auth/identifiers/verify` accepts the code. A second code to the same normalized address within the resend interval is a 429 throttled; the window is held against the address and shared across sessions and accounts. The call requires the fresh authentication every change of what proves the account asks for and refuses an impersonating identity; a write rotates the caller's session token and revokes the account's other sessions. A login name or address another account holds is a 409 conflict, and a deployment with no email channel answers the email branch with 503 unavailable.

requestBody.description: The login identifier to add: its kind and its value. The body must be `application/json` and refuses unknown members.

schema.description: The login identifier to add: a username or an email address.

kind.description: The identifier kind to add: username or email; a phone is added through /auth/phone

value.description: The login name or address to add. A username is NFKC-normalized and lowercased first, then accepted only when it is 3 to 64 characters of [a-z0-9._-] beginning with a letter or a digit and does not carry the reserved static-credential prefix; the stored value is the normalized one. An email address is trimmed and lowercased first, then accepted only when it is ASCII, contains exactly one `@` with no whitespace, and is at most 254 bytes; anything else is a 400 bad-request.

200.description: A username was added; or a code was sent to an address and its answer is still to come

400.description: The body could not be read, or the kind or the value is outside its domain

401.description: No usable credential, or the freshness a change of what proves the account asks for

403.description: The identity is impersonating, which the route refuses

409.description: The login name or address belongs to another account

415.description: The request body is not application/json

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

503.description: A dependency could not answer, or the deployment offers no email channel

post.summary: Verify the code sent to an email address being added
post.description: Accepts the code sent to an email address being added and, on a match, writes the address as an identifier verified by that code. The pending address and the code's digest are read from the server-side record of the caller's session, so the client submits only the code and cannot choose which address is verified. A missing record, one that names another account, or one that does not parse is a 401 flow-invalid. A wrong code is a 401 login-failed; five wrong codes for one issued code spend the pending verification, and the record also expires with the code's lifetime. On success the record is consumed, the caller's session token is rotated, the account's other sessions are revoked, and the answer is 200 with `state: added`.

requestBody.description: The code the email channel delivered to the address being added. The body must be `application/json` and refuses unknown members.

schema.description: The code sent to the email address being added.

code.description: The six-digit code the email channel delivered, as a string. Empty or longer than 32 bytes is a 400 bad-request; a wrong code is a 401 login-failed, and five wrong codes for one issued code spend the pending verification.

200.description: The address was verified and added to the account

400.description: The body could not be read, or the code is empty or longer than 32 bytes

401.description: No usable credential, or no pending verification for this session

403.description: The identity is impersonating, which the route refuses

409.description: The address belongs to another account

415.description: The request body is not application/json

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

delete.summary: Unbind one of the caller's own external identities
delete.description: Unbinds one external identity from the caller's account. The binding must be the caller's own; one that is not, whether it does not exist or belongs to another account, is a 400 bad-request. The call requires the fresh authentication every change of what proves the account asks for — a multi-factor assurance merely declared by an identity provider does not count — and refuses an impersonating identity. The account module refuses to remove the last way to sign in (409 conflict); a way only an identity provider declared does not count as a way to sign in, which is why this route asks for local freshness. On success the call publishes `authn.binding.changed` when the provider is in the event payload's closed set, rotates the caller's session token, revokes the account's other sessions, and answers 204.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The external binding's identifier, as returned in the `id` of one of the caller's own external identities. A value the caller's account does not hold is a 400 bad-request.

403.description: The identity is impersonating, which the route refuses

409.description: The binding is the account's last way in

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

AuthnLoginMethods.description: The discovery document of the login surface: one descriptor per login method that takes part and is not turned off, whether a first login may open an account, and the second-factor kinds the deployment takes in. Enterprise identity providers are not listed here; they are discovered through the SSO module.

methods.description: The methods taking part that are not turned off, one descriptor each, sorted by name

signup.description: Whether a first login may open an account on this deployment.

mfa.description: The second-factor kinds the deployment takes in.

AuthnMethodDescriptor.description: One login method as the discovery document reports it: its stable name, how a client renders it, the protocol a redirect or enterprise method speaks, its brand label, whether it can open an account, and the inputs its first step asks for.

kind.description: How a client renders the method: form, redirect, enterprise or webauthn

protocol.description: The wire protocol a redirect or enterprise method speaks: oauth2, oidc or saml; empty otherwise

label.description: The method's brand name where it has one, otherwise empty for a name-keyed translation

opens_account.description: Whether the method may open an account for an identifier it does not yet know

fields.description: The inputs the method's first step asks for, empty for a method that does not open with a form

AuthnLoginSignup.description: Whether a first login may open an account on this deployment, derived from the account module's signup switch. A closed switch does not remove a method; it only makes a first login for an unknown identifier fail.

enabled.description: Whether a first login may open an account

AuthnLoginMFA.description: The second-factor kinds the deployment takes in, as the multi-factor module reports them. This is a deployment-level list, not the caller's own registered factors.

factors.description: The kinds of second factor the deployment takes in

AuthnLoginFlow.description: One open login flow, as returned by a start, by an answer that keeps the flow open, or by the current-flow read: the step number the next answer must echo, the flow's state, the flow token when the flow is bound by the header, and what the client does next.

seq.description: The step number the next answer must echo

state.description: The flow's state: first, second, enroll, ready, processing, done or failed

flow_token.description: The flow token, set only when the flow is bound by the Authn-Flow header

next.description: What the client does at the flow's current step.

AuthnLoginStep.description: What the client does at the flow's current step. Only the members that belong to `kind` are present: `challenge` carries `fields`; `redirect` carries `url` and `method`; `factor` carries `factors`; `enroll` carries `kinds`; `webauthn` carries `options`; `complete` carries nothing.

kind.description: What the client does next: challenge, redirect, factor, enroll, complete or webauthn

fields.description: The inputs a challenge step asks for

expires_in.description: How long a challenge lives, in seconds. No handler of this fragment sets it, so the member is absent from every answer.

resend_after.description: How soon a challenge may be asked for again, in seconds. No handler of this fragment sets it, so the member is absent from every answer.

url.description: Where a redirect step sends the user agent

method.description: The HTTP method the redirect uses

factors.description: The factors a second-factor step offers

kinds.description: The factor kinds an enroll step takes in

options.description: The data a webauthn step carries: the public-key creation or request options of a WebAuthn ceremony, or, for a TOTP enrollment, an object with an `otpauth_uri` the client renders as a QR code.

AuthnLoginField.description: One input a method asks the client for, named by the method and rendered according to its kind.

name.description: The input's key: the client submits its value under this name in the `input` map of the start request or of the answer.

kind.description: How the client renders the input: `text`, `password`, `code` or `phone`.

required.description: Whether the step needs a value; absent means the field may be left out.

secret.description: Whether the value must not be displayed or echoed, as for a password or a code; absent means it is not secret.

AuthnLoginFactor.description: One second factor the flow offers to verify: its identifier, its kind and a display label. It carries nothing secret.

id.description: The factor's identifier; send it as `input.factor` when answering the second-factor step.

kind.description: The factor kind, such as `totp`, `sms` or `webauthn`; the client renders the challenge according to it.

label.description: A display label for the factor; it may be empty, in which case the client falls back to the kind's own name.

AuthnLoginSession.description: The answer of a login completed with `delivery=session`, and of a step-up completed on a cookie session: the state name `authenticated` and the public facts of the session that was created or elevated. The session cookie is set in the same response.

state.description: The literal `authenticated`, marking a completed login.

session.description: The public facts of the session the login created.

AuthnLoginSessionView.description: The public facts of the session a login created. No token or secret is included.

id.description: The session identifier; the browser client holds the session cookie written in the same response.

expires_at.description: The session's expiry as an RFC 3339 instant, or empty

AuthnLoginToken.description: The answer of a login completed with `delivery=token`, and of a token-delivered step-up: the state name, the token type, the access token, its lifetime and the refresh token.

state.description: authenticated for a login; elevated for a step-up, which issues no refresh token and carries it empty

token_type.description: The authorization scheme the access token is sent with; it is always `Bearer`.

access_token.description: The access token, sent in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer <value>`.

expires_in.description: The access token's lifetime in seconds

refresh_token.description: Empty on a step-up, which issues no refresh token

AuthnLoginActionResult.description: The answer of a flow that finished by binding an external identity (`linked`) or registering a factor (`enrolled`); neither issues a session or a token.

state.description: linked when the flow bound an external identity; enrolled when it registered a factor

AuthnLoginPhoneChallenge.description: The answer to a phone-verification send: how long the code lives and how soon another code may be asked for, both in whole seconds. It carries neither the challenge identifier nor any fact about whether the number is already held by another account.

expires_in.description: How long the code lives, in seconds

resend_after.description: How soon another code may be asked for, in seconds

AuthnLoginIdentifierState.description: The answer of adding an identifier: `added` when the identifier is written, `pending` when a code was sent to an email address and the answer is still to come. The two durations are present only in the pending state.

state.description: added when the identifier is written; pending when a code was sent to an address and its answer is still to come

expires_in.description: How long the code lives, in seconds; absent when the state is added

resend_after.description: How soon another code may be asked for, in seconds; absent when the state is added

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. This is the entry point's default error shape, which a host-supplied ErrorResponder may replace.

type.description: The machine-readable code identifying the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the RFC 9457 default about:blank; codes this platform defines are URNs of the form urn:speed:<capability>:<code>.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the standard English status text for the status code.

status.description: The HTTP status code the response is written with, repeated from the status line.

detail.description: A longer explanation of this occurrence, present only when the answering module has one to give. It may be a sentence rendered in the request language or a language-neutral token such as "forbidden", so clients must not parse it.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence; absent when there is none to give.
